newsitem.title: UK: LME tin claws back some lost ground in late trade.
newsitem.headline: LME tin claws back some lost ground in late trade.

text.p: LME tin prices failed to recover much of the ground lost during an earlier fund-led selling bout in late inter-office trading on Thursday after another stocks rise sparked bearish sentiment.

Earlier, three months tin slumped to its lowest in over two years, hitting $5,580 per tonne -- the lowest since March 1995 -- as fund liquidation took its toll in the wake of a 400-tonne stocks rise and shaky technicals
Tin was indicated at $5,580/5,600 at 1812 GMT and was little changed from the $5,600 kerb close, which represented a $65 loss on the day.
Copper was indicated at $2,530/31 after a stock fall of 3,550 tonnes drove prices up to $2,537 earlier in the day -- within a whisker of Wednesday's peak.
